subject: Intermittent connection failures during private cutover — conntrack sync loss
messages:
From: infra-eng@clearbridge-health.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: network-ops@clearbridge-health.com
Date: 2028-07-29 09:12 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 502s from private nodes after cutover

Hi Grace / Vanessa,

We started the private cutover at 03:00 PT and are seeing intermittent connection failures from our on-prem services to Redwood Private gateways. Symptoms: short-lived TCP resets and long tails on POSTs to the inference endpoint (p95 ~ 2.8s), followed by successful retries. The pattern started 10m after cutover and repeats every ~30-90m for ~5-10 minutes.

We grabbed conntrack dumps and a short pcap when it next hit — attaching both. Can you advise whether this looks like SNAT port exhaustion or an asymmetric return path?

Quick details:
- Cutover: routed through hybrid-gateway A -> Redwood Private edge (us-west-2)
- MTU on our edge: 1500, no jumbo frames configured
- Security groups: we allow 443/80 inbound from our subnets to the gateway

We can open a maintenance window if you need deeper tracing.

Thanks,
Dave Tang
Infra Engineer
ClearBridge Health

Attachments: conntrack-dump-20280729.txt (text), tcpdump-private-cutover.pcap (pcap)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: infra-eng@clearbridge-health.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 09:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from private nodes after cutover

Thanks Dave — got the dumps and the pcap. First-pass observations: I see a burst of SYN -> SYN-ACK -> RST sequences interleaved with normal traffic. Conntrack shows a high number of TIME_WAIT / close-wait entries for ephemeral ports around the time of spikes.

Plan:
- Karthik/Rishi: can you confirm whether our edge SNAT pool is being recycled aggressively during the cutover? I want to rule out port churn from our side.
- Vanessa: can you check routing asymmetry (BGP / next-hop) and whether return path traverses a different intermediate that could be dropping fragments?
- Dave: can you confirm whether clients behind your on-prem NAT are reusing ephemeral ports aggressively (e.g., short client connect timeouts)?

If this is conntrack table saturation we can temporarily increase ephemeral port range and conntrack table size, but we'd prefer to understand root cause first.

I'll stand by on Zoom for 30m to debug if you want.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Support Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 10:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from private nodes after cutover

Adding what I can from the runtime side. I pulled SNAT/conntrack metrics for the timeframe: there's a visible uptick in conntrack entries ~8–12m after the cutover, peaking at ~78% of table capacity for the private edge. The SNAT ephemeral port allocation shows increased churn but not exhaustion.

Hypothesis: conntrack table saturation from short-lived parallel connections (clients + retries) combined with asymmetric return paths causing delayed FIN/ACK processing -> stale entries. That will manifest as resets when conntrack can't reconcile state.

Immediate mitigations we can try (in order):
1) Increase conntrack_max to 1.5x current for the private-edge fleet (non-disruptive param change).
2) Expand SNAT port range for the edge pool by 10k ports for the window.
3) Temporarily enable SYN cookies / reduce keepalive timeouts if we see SYN floods (unlikely).

I agree we should also validate MTU and fragmentation handling; the pcap shows occasional IP fragments for larger payloads (likely TLS records + HTTP/2 frames). If the intermediate path occasionally drops fragments or reorders them, that could cause session failures we see.

I'll prepare a quick runbook for 1–2 and coordinate a safe window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: dave.tang@clearbridge-health.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: network-ops@clearbridge-health.com
Date: 2028-07-29 12:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from private nodes after cutover

Thanks — we validated client side: our services are reusing ports aggressively (short-lived clients spawned by autoscaling jobs). We can throttle retries for a window but cannot change how ephemeral ports are used quickly.

We also ran traceroutes and see that return traffic sometimes takes a different transit (via partner-peering) with a hop that performs PMTU blackhole behaviour (drops fragments >1300).

We'll schedule a short maintenance window at 15:30 PT to allow you to make config changes. Attaching additional conntrack dumps captured during the 12:04 spike.

Dave

Attachments: conntrack-dump-2-20280729.txt
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: dave.tang@clearbridge-health.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 14:48 -0700
Subject: Action plan for 15:30 maintenance — conntrack and MTU mitigations

Action summary for 15:30 PT maintenance window (agreed with ClearBridge):

1) Increase conntrack_max on the private-edge fleet from 524288 -> 786432 (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max) — expected immediate reduction in saturation errors. (Karthik)
2) Expand SNAT port range on the edge pool by +10000 ports and bump ephemeral port range on the edge backend (Rishi).
3) Add a temporary iptables rule to drop fragmented packets with DF cleared to force PMTU discovery fallback for a subset of hosts (Vanessa) — only applied to canary hostset of 10 nodes to limit blast radius.
4) Monitor conntrack usage, SNAT port allocation, and 5xx rate. Rollback changes if 5xx increases or latency degradations observed.

Notes / checks:
- Dave: confirm the canary hostset IPs and keep network-ops on call.
- Marissa: prep incident banner and update status page if we need a wider rollback.

I'll apply steps 1 and 2 at 15:30, Vanessa will apply step 3 to canary, Rishi will watch SNAT counters. We'll meet on Zoom (link in calendar) at 15:20 to verify.

— Grace
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: dave.tang@clearbridge-health.com
Date: 2028-07-29 16:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from private nodes after cutover — resolved on canary

Post-maintenance update: canary changes showed immediate improvement. Conntrack usage dropped to ~42% of capacity on canary nodes, SNAT port churn reduced, and ClearBridge reports no 502s in the last 25m for canary IPs.

We rolled the conntrack_max and SNAT port expansion cluster-wide by 15:55. Vanessa's canary-frag rule revealed that the partner-peering hop indeed dropped fragments >1300 — we'll follow up with ClearBridge to patch PMTU or add MTU-friendly tunnel encapsulation on their side.

Action items completed / next steps:
- Follow-up ticket to ClearBridge network team to remediate partner peering PMTU (assigned NET-4521).
- Keep conntrack_max at +50% and monitor for 72h (Karthik/Rishi).
- Incident summary + RCA draft (Grace/Marissa) due EOD tomorrow.

Thanks everyone for quick coordination.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
